Risk Management Plan (RMP) - Propane
Executive Summary
Superior Fuel Company
5020 Lesure Street, Duluth, Minnesota

Superior Fuel Company has been safely handling propane since 2006.  Superior Fuel Company is committed to maintaining the highest levels of safety and operational performance at this facility.  This terminal operates with the attention to detail necessary to maintain the terminal safety systems, operator activity and training, and safety performance Superior Fuel Company is accustomed to. 

Description of the Stationary Source and Regulated Substances

This facility receives propane from rail tank cars at a tank car unloading facility.  The tank cars are switched by terminal operator and unloaded into the terminal fixed tanks.  The propane is stored on site in fixed propane storage tanks.  The terminal is a fully automated terminal and is available for 24-hour truck loading by trained and qualified drivers.  The terminal is equipped with multiple security systems so that only qualified and authorized drivers can gain access to the terminal and loading operations.  In this process, the terminal stores the following chemicals that the EPA has identified as having the potential to cause significant offsite consequences in the event of a substantial accidental release.  

Toxics:
There are no listed toxic substances above EPA threshold quantitates

Flammables:
Propane, CAS-74-98-6

1.  Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies

We at Superior Fuel Company are strongly committed to employee, public, and environmental safety.  This commitment is an inherent part of our comprehensive accidental release prevention program that covers areas such as design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training associated with the processes at our facility.  It is our policy to implement appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of regulated substances.  We coordinate our response efforts with the St Louis County Emerg

ency Management Agency and the Duluth City Fire Department, which provides additional emergency response expertise.

2.  Stationary Source and Regulated Substances Handled

Our facility's primary activities include support services for fueling and heating.  We have propane stored in four 80,000-gallon tanks (320,000 total storage gallons), which is approximately 1,344,000 lbs.  However, the maximum  stored at the facility is 85% standard maximum storage capacity.

3.  Worst Case Release and Alternative Release Scenarios

We utilized RMP Comp for the worst case and alternate case scenarios of the required offsite consequence analysis for our facility.

4.  General Accidental Release Prevention Program

Our facility has taken all the necessary steps to comply with the EPA's accidental release prevention requirements as set forth in 40 CFR part 68.  The following sections briefly describe the elements of the release prevention program that is in place at our stationary source.

Process Safety Information

Superior Fuel Company maintains a detailed record of safety information that describes the chemical hazards, operating parameters, and equipment designs associated with all processes.

Process Hazard Analysis

Our facility conducts comprehensive studies to ensure that hazards associated with our processes are identified and controlled effectively.  Any findings from the hazard analysis are addressed in a timely manner.

Operating Procedures

Superior Fuel Company maintains written operating procedures to ensure that activities within our covered processes are conducted safely.  These procedures address various modes of operation; the information is regularly reviewed and is readily accessible to operators involved in the processes.

Training

Superior Fuel Company has a comprehensive training program in place to ensure that employees who are operating processes are competent in the operating procedures associated with these processes.

Mechanical Integrity

Superior F

uel Company conducts documented maintenance checks on process equipment to ensure proper operation. Maintenance checks are conducted by qualified personnel with previous training in maintenance practices.  Examples of process equipment that would receive maintenance checks include:  pressure vessels, storage tanks, piping systems, relief and vent systems, emergency shutdown systems, controls, and pumps.  Any equipment deficiencies identified by the maintenance checks are corrected in a safe and timely manner.

Management of Change

Written procedures are in place at Superior Fuel Company to manage changes in process chemicals, technology, equipment, and procedures.  Process operators, maintenance personnel or other employees whose job tasks are affected by a modification in process conditions are promptly notified of the modification and offered training to deal with it.

Pre-startup Reviews

Superior Fuel Company routinely conducts pre-startup safety reviews related to new processes and modifications in established processes.  These reviews are conducted to confirm that construction, equipment, and operating and maintenance procedures are suitable for safe startup prior to placing equipment into operation.

Compliance Audits

Superior Fuel Company conducts compliance audits on a regular basis to determine whether the plan's provisions, set out under the 40 CFR part 68, are being implemented.  Any non-compliance issue discovered during the audit is promptly corrected.

Employee Participation

Superior Fuel Company truly believes that process safety management and accident prevention is a team effort. Company employees are strongly encouraged to express their views concerning accident prevention issues and to recommend improvements.  In addition, our employees have access to all information created as part of the facility's implementation of the RMP, particularly information resulting from process hazard analyses.

5.  Five-year Accident History

Superior Fuel Compan

y has had an excellent record of preventing accidental releases over the last 5 years.  Due to our stringent release prevention policies, no accidental release has occurred during this period.

6.  Emergency Action Plan

Superior Fuel Company maintains a written emergency action plan to deal with accidental releases of hazardous materials.  The plan addresses all aspects of emergency response including first aid and medical treatment, evacuations, and in the event of an accidental release, Superior Fuel Company will contact local emergency response agencies and the public.  Superior Fuel Company maintains a written emergency action plan which is coordinated with the local fire department and the LEPC.  The plan is intended to assist responding agencies to address all aspects of emergency response including first aid and medical treatment, evacuations, and notification of local emergency response agencies and the public.

7.  Planned Changes to Improve Safety

We will continue to provide our employees with ongoing annual training to ensure that they are current with all of the safe propane transfer and handling procedures, and provide regular inspection and maintenance on all of the propane equipment.  Authorized personnel will make changes to the facility if any audits of the facility identify non-compliance with Section 112
 (r)(7), Accidental Release Prevention Requirements of the Clean Air Act.
